esrchReview.trigger: The first task query must return exactly zero bytes and ESRCH, followed by a full valid live BSD identity matching UID/group and any externally expected generation. Other failures do not trigger the additional read.
esrchReview.bound: Exactly one immediate call to _read_once; no sleep, recursion or widening of the existing three group samples and two 0.25-second sleeps.
esrchReview.identity: The fallback full birth is an internal reconciliation anchor. The external owned-generation expectation remains separate. A recovered measured result must retain the same internal birth and all original resource validations.
esrchReview.replacement: A new live or zombie generation cannot be excluded through the internal anchor; it remains unknown. Only replacement of an externally expected owned generation retains the existing gone meaning.
esrchReview.disappearance: Same-birth authoritative zombie or independent ESRCH may reconcile absence. ESRCH or flags alone do not imply disappearance.
esrchReview.uncertainty: Persistent live ESRCH, permission, invalid/short identity, wrong owner/group and invalid counters remain unavailable; no unknown RSS/CPU becomes zero.
esrchReview.singleReadValidationAST: The former read body equals _read_once after removing the two internal birth assignments and renaming the function. Existing task/BSD validation logic is unchanged.
esrchReview.diagnosticBounds: Per-group recheck count plus at most three examples; successful reconciliation enters the existing most-recent-16 retention. Reconciliation resets the progress watcher rather than treating an unobserved interval as stall evidence.

failureEvidenceReview.publicContent: Only fixed message-kind enums, Rust Edddd codes, relative tail-line indices, counts, sizes and truncation/availability fields. No original free text, paths, identifiers, quoted values, argv, environment or exception messages are copied.
failureEvidenceReview.inputBounds: Each snapshot reads at most 131072 bytes of a regular file, refuses symlinks and non-regular files, and opens nonblocking to avoid a FIFO hang.
failureEvidenceReview.recordBounds: At most 16 retained shapes: all when within the cap, otherwise the first eight and last eight.
failureEvidenceReview.chronology: Failure snapshots are taken before cleanup where possible and separately after cleanup. A failure first discovered during cleanup records beforeCleanup unavailable/not-captured-before-cleanup.
failureEvidenceReview.failureIsolation: Both snapshot call sites catch ordinary collector exceptions and return a fixed diagnostic-collector-error record. Original Failure, firstFailure, phase, stage record, cleanup result and exact child reap remain preserved.
failureEvidenceReview.markerMeaning: The broad compiler-error text counter becomes error-marker, explicitly scoped as post-cleanup text matches rather than a compiler-failure verdict.
failureEvidenceReview.limit: These are canonical substring classifications, not verbatim diagnostic excerpts or proof of cause. Unclassified, colored, truncated or unsupported diagnostics may lose details.

closedReviewPoints.topic: Internal generation anchor could discard a new group member
closedReviewPoints.resolution: New same-PID/different-birth live and zombie results remain unknown unless an external expected owned generation was replaced; group regression requires null totals and zero confirmed-gone increment.

closedReviewPoints.topic: Cleanup-only failure could mislabel later output as before cleanup
closedReviewPoints.resolution: Explicit unavailable pre-cleanup marker and regression through prepared cleanup failure.

closedReviewPoints.topic: A throwing collector could replace the primary failure or suppress its stage record
closedReviewPoints.resolution: Fixed unavailable conversion at both collector boundaries plus a real Linux monitor-stop regression injecting a secret-bearing exception.
